project.projectDesc: Adds phone-based speech input and spoken responses to restaurant ordering, with escalation to staff when automation needs help.

caseStudy.summary: This voice-ordering system lets restaurant customers place phone orders through spoken conversation. I extended the text-ordering workflow with speech recognition, restaurant vocabulary adaptation, spoken responses, and a transfer path to restaurant staff.
caseStudy.challenge: Phone ordering introduces recognition errors from accents, background noise, menu terminology, quantities, and ambiguous instructions. The system needed to reuse the existing order-understanding logic while preserving a human fallback when a call could not be completed confidently.
caseStudy.architecture: The call channel converts speech to text, sends the transcript through the restaurant-ordering NLP system, and converts the response back to speech. Calls that need human assistance can be transferred to restaurant staff.
caseStudy.diagram:
flowchart LR
  Caller[Restaurant caller] --> ASR[Speech recognition]
  ASR --> NLP[Text-ordering engine]
  NLP --> Order[Structured order]
  Order --> POS[Restaurant order flow]
  NLP --> TTS[Spoken response]
  TTS --> Caller
  ASR -->|Needs assistance| Staff[Restaurant staff]
contributions: Extended the text-ordering product to support phone-based conversational orders.
Adapted speech recognition using restaurant text, menu terms, food vocabulary, and varied accents.
Connected call handling, transcription, order interpretation, and spoken responses.
Added a fallback path for transferring customers to restaurant staff.
tradeoffs: Reusing the text-ordering engine avoids duplicating menu and order logic, while speech recognition introduces a separate source of uncertainty.
A human transfer path preserves customer choice and supports calls that are noisy, ambiguous, or outside the bot flow.
Real-time voice interactions balance conversational speed with confirmation and staff transfer for ambiguous orders.

business: Phone-based voice offers a channel alongside text and web ordering.
quality: Human transfer provides a recovery path for recognition and conversation failures.
